herringgull: A herring gull standing, a large heavy gull with a clean WHITE HEAD AND BODY, PALE SILVER-GREY BACK AND WINGS, and BLACK WINGTIPS SPOTTED WITH WHITE. Its bill is heavy, yellow and hooked slightly at the tip, carrying a SINGLE ROUND ORANGE-RED SPOT LOW ON THE LOWER MANDIBLE. Its eye is pale yellow with a hard staring look, and its legs are dull pink.
bluemussel: A blue mussel, a bivalve with a smooth glossy WEDGE-SHAPED SHELL, pointed and slightly curved at the hinge end and broadly rounded at the other, its surface a deep blue-black shading to violet and marked with fine concentric growth lines. The shell gapes slightly, showing a pale cream mantle edge and a bundle of FINE TOUGH GOLDEN-BROWN ANCHORING THREADS at the pointed end.
acornbarnacle: An acorn barnacle, a small marine animal shaped like a low volcano cone about the width of a fingernail, built of SIX HARD CHALKY OFF-WHITE PLATES fused into a ridged circular wall with a DIAMOND-SHAPED OPENING AT THE SUMMIT closed by two pairs of moving doors. From the opening a FAN OF FINE CURLED FEATHERY LEGS reaches out. A single animal alone.
giantgreenanemone: A giant green anemone, a sea anemone with a thick smooth COLUMN like a squat cylinder and a broad flat oral disc at the top, ringed by SEVERAL DENSE ROWS OF SHORT BLUNT POINTED TENTACLES packed close together like a shaggy crown. Its colour is a vivid GRASS-GREEN to emerald across the disc and tentacles, the column paler and olive-drab, with a small slit mouth at the centre.
aldabragianttortoise: An Aldabra giant tortoise walking, an enormous tortoise with a HIGH DOMED SLATE-GREY SHELL divided into large plates, its neck long and extended forward. Its legs are the point: THICK, STRAIGHT, COLUMN-LIKE AND HEAVILY ARMOURED IN COARSE OVERLAPPING SCALES, held directly beneath the body like an elephant's, with blunt stumpy toes and short nails. Small blunt head, dark eyes.
littlebluepenguin: A little blue penguin standing, THE SMALLEST PENGUIN, only about the height of a ruler, so it reads as tiny and slightly hunched. Its back and flippers are a distinctive SLATE BLUE-GREY WITH A FAINT INDIGO SHEEN rather than black, its front and throat are clean white, and it has a slim dark grey bill, small pale eyes and pale pink feet.
staghorncoral: A staghorn coral colony, a stony coral whose skeleton grows as MANY STRAIGHT CYLINDRICAL ROUNDED ARMS that divide and re-divide upward and outward into an open spreading thicket, each arm ending in a slightly paler rounded tip. Its surface is covered in a fine regular texture of TINY CUP-SHAPED PITS. Warm golden tan and honey-brown. A colony of animals, absolutely NOT antlers and NOT a plant.
braincoral: A brain coral colony, a stony coral forming a LARGE SOLID ROUNDED BOULDER-SHAPED DOME, its entire surface covered by DEEP WINDING PARALLEL GROOVES AND RIDGES that meander and fold back on themselves in an unbroken maze. Ridges pale cream-tan, valleys darker olive-brown, with fine perpendicular cross-lines. A colony of animals, absolutely NOT an actual brain and NOT an organ.
giantclam: A giant clam, an enormous bivalve with a HEAVY THICK-WALLED SHELL whose two halves meet in a DEEPLY ZIGZAGGED WAVY LIP like interlocking teeth, the outside chalky white and marked with several broad radiating fluted ribs. The shell gapes wide, and between the halves swells a THICK FLESHY MANTLE OF ELECTRIC BLUE, TURQUOISE AND GOLD-GREEN, patterned with fine iridescent spots.
pistolshrimp: A pistol shrimp, a small stout shrimp with a semi-transparent orange-banded body, short antennae and small stalked eyes, whose ONE CLAW IS ENORMOUSLY ENLARGED, nearly as large as the whole rest of its body, heavy and blocky with a PRONOUNCED PIVOTING HAMMER ON THE UPPER JAW cocked open. Its other claw is tiny and ordinary by comparison.
humpheadwrasse: A humphead wrasse, a very large heavy-bodied reef fish in vivid electric blue-green, its scales each carrying a fine pale outline so the flank reads as a net of turquoise. Its face is the point: THICK RUBBERY LIPS, a pair of BLACK DIAGONAL LINES BEHIND EACH EYE, and a LARGE ROUNDED BULGING HUMP SWELLING FROM ITS FOREHEAD ABOVE THE EYES in the adult male.
kangaroorat: A kangaroo rat, a small sandy-buff rodent built for hopping, with VERY LARGE POWERFUL HIND LEGS AND TINY SHORT FOREPAWS held tucked at the chest, sitting upright on its haunches. It has a BIG BLUNT HEAD WITH ENORMOUS DARK EYES, external FUR-LINED CHEEK POUCHES, and a TAIL LONGER THAN ITS BODY ending in a CONSPICUOUS TUFT OF LONG HAIRS like a flag.
namibdesertbeetle: A Namib desert beetle, a stout black beetle standing HEAD-DOWN WITH ITS REAR END TILTED HIGH IN THE AIR on long stilt-like legs. Its fused wing cases form a SMOOTH HARD DOMED SHELL, matte black and covered in a FINE REGULAR PATTERN OF SMALL RAISED BUMPS, with shallow waxy channels running between them toward the head. Short elbowed antennae.
mexicanredknee: A Mexican redknee tarantula, a large hairy tarantula with a DARK BLACK-BROWN BODY AND A TAN-CREAM CARAPACE outlined in black, standing squarely on eight thick legs. The marking that names it: the JOINTS OF EVERY LEG ARE BANDED IN VIVID BURNT ORANGE-RED against the black, forming bright rings at each knee. Dense bristly hairs cover its abdomen and legs.
egyptianvulture: An Egyptian vulture standing, a SMALL slim white vulture with black flight feathers, and a distinctive head: the FACE AND THROAT ARE BARE WRINKLED SKIN OF BRIGHT ORANGE-YELLOW, and the crown and nape carry a SHAGGY SPIKY RUFF OF LOOSE WHITE FEATHERS standing out like an untidy mane. Its bill is slender, hooked and yellow with a dark tip. Wedge-shaped tail.
bumblebeebat: A bumblebee bat, THE SMALLEST BAT AND ONE OF THE SMALLEST MAMMALS, ABOUT THE SIZE AND WEIGHT OF A LARGE BUMBLEBEE, so it reads as astonishingly tiny. It has a distinctive PIG-LIKE SNOUT with a swollen fleshy nose-pad and wide nostrils, LARGE RELATIVELY BIG EARS with a slender pointed inner flap, tiny eyes, and reddish-brown fur. Sitting upright, wings folded close against the body.
woodfrog: A wood frog, a small slim frog with smooth skin in warm tan, rust and pinkish-brown, a pale cream belly and a fine pale line along the upper lip. The marking that identifies it: a BOLD DARK CHOCOLATE-BROWN ROBBER'S MASK RUNNING FROM THE SNOUT BACK THROUGH EACH EYE AND OVER THE EARDRUM, ending sharply at the shoulder. Raised ridges run down each side of its back.
iberianlynx: An Iberian lynx standing, a medium cat noticeably smaller and shorter-bodied than other lynxes, with a bright tawny-yellow coat MARKED ALL OVER IN BOLD DISTINCT DARK BROWN SPOTS. Its face carries a PRONOUNCED FLARED RUFF OF LONG SIDE-WHISKERS hanging below the cheeks like a beard, LONG BLACK TUFTS RISING FROM THE EAR TIPS, and it has very long legs and a short black-tipped tail.
indiangiantsquirrel: An Indian giant squirrel, an ENORMOUS tree squirrel NEARLY A METRE FROM NOSE TO TAIL TIP, far larger than any common squirrel. Its coat is boldly two-toned: DEEP MAROON-PURPLE AND RUST-ORANGE OVER THE BACK AND THE LONG BUSHY TAIL, with CREAM-WHITE underparts and forelimbs, and a pale ring around each large dark eye. Rounded ears with small tufts.
gemsbok: A gemsbok standing, a large heavy antelope with a pale fawn-grey body, and the boldest face pattern of any antelope: a STARK BLACK-AND-WHITE MASK with a black blaze down the nose, black cheek bands and a white face beneath. A BLACK STRIPE RUNS ALONG EACH FLANK dividing fawn from white, and its HORNS ARE VERY LONG, PERFECTLY STRAIGHT, SLENDER AND RINGED, rising in a shallow V.
greaterhoneyguide: A greater honeyguide, a plain sparrow-sized bird in drab olive-grey and brown with a paler belly, WHITE OUTER TAIL FEATHERS showing at the sides, and a SHORT STUBBY PALE PINK BILL. The adult male carries a BLACK THROAT PATCH and a BRIGHT WHITE PATCH ON EACH CHEEK below the eye, with a small golden-yellow shoulder mark on the folded wing.
northernpike: A northern pike, a long low torpedo-shaped predatory fish with its SINGLE BACK FIN SET VERY FAR BACK CLOSE TO THE TAIL, opposite the anal fin. Its head is the point: LONG, BROAD AND FLATTENED INTO A DUCK-BILL SHAPE with a wide mouth full of long backward-slanting teeth. Olive-green flanks scattered with ROWS OF PALE CREAM BEAN-SHAPED SPOTS, a cream belly.
electriceel: An electric eel, a LONG THICK CYLINDRICAL FISH shaped like an eel but not one, with a BLUNT ROUNDED HEAD, a wide flat mouth and small eyes. It has NO BACK FIN AT ALL; instead A SINGLE VERY LONG RIPPLING FIN RUNS ALONG THE ENTIRE UNDERSIDE from throat to tail tip, and the tail makes up most of its length. Slate grey-brown above, ORANGE-YELLOW ACROSS THE THROAT AND CHIN.
